database_summary: This is a normalized OLTP-style product/order/customer schema (Northwind-like) implemented in SQLite. It contains entity tables for products, customers, suppliers, shippers, employees, categories, territories/region, and US states, plus transactional/event tables orders and order_details, a bridge table employeeterritories, and small lookup/threshold tables. Row counts indicate moderate historic orders (orders 830, order_details 2155). Many tables store descriptive attributes; orders and order_details represent events/transactions. Watch joins between orders/order_details/products/customers/employees which can multiply rows (one order -> many details).

accepted.name: orders_with_line_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT od.orderid,
       od.productid,
       od.unitprice,
       od.quantity,
       od.discount,
       (od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0))) AS line_total,
       o.customerid,
       o.employeeid,
       o.orderdate,
       o.requireddate,
       o.shippeddate,
       o.shipvia,
       o.freight,
       o.shipcountry,
       p.productname,
       p.supplierid,
       p.categoryid,
       c.companyname AS companyname,
       e.lastname AS lastname,
       e.firstname AS firstname
FROM order_details od
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.orderid = od.orderid
LEFT JOIN products p ON p.productid = od.productid
LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customerid = o.customerid
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.employeeid = o.employeeid
accepted.description: One row per order line enriched with order and product/customer/employee attributes and a derived line_total (unitprice * quantity * (1-discount)). Useful as a reusable denormalized order-line view for revenue, product performance, customer purchase, and employee sales analyses. | Use for: Total revenue by order / product / customer / employee; Order-line level profitability or revenue trends; Join-ready denormalized order lines for filtering by date, product, customer, or employee

accepted.name: orders_agg_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT od.orderid,
       COUNT(*) AS total_lines,
       SUM(od.quantity) AS total_quantity,
       SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0))) AS total_amount,
       AVG(od.unitprice) AS avg_unitprice
FROM order_details od
GROUP BY od.orderid
accepted.description: One row per order aggregating its order lines to produce order-level measures: total_lines, total_quantity, total_amount (sum of line totals) and average_unitprice. Useful for analyses at the order (transaction) grain: order value distribution, average basket size, and joining back to customers/employees/shippers. | Use for: Which orders are highest value or largest by quantity; Order-level KPIs such as average basket size or order amount; Segmenting orders by total_amount or total_quantity

accepted.name: product_inventory_snapshot
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT p.productid,
       p.productname,
       p.supplierid,
       p.categoryid,
       COALESCE(p.quantityperunit, '') AS quantityperunit,
       COALESCE(p.unitprice, 0.0) AS unitprice,
       COALESCE(p.unitsinstock, 0) AS unitsinstock,
       COALESCE(p.unitsonorder, 0) AS unitsonorder,
       COALESCE(p.reorderlevel, 0) AS reorderlevel,
       p.discontinued
FROM products p
accepted.description: One row per product exposing inventory and pricing attributes cleaned/coalesced. Useful for product catalogue, stock-level alerts, and joining to sales to compute stock coverage. Provides explicit numeric defaults where NULLs might appear. | Use for: Inventory level reports and stock reordering alerts; Price lists and product catalog exports; Joining product attributes to sales to compute stock-to-sales ratios

accepted.name: customer_order_counts_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT c.customerid,
       c.companyname,
       COALESCE(oagg.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders,
       COALESCE(oagg.total_amount, 0.0) AS total_amount,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(oagg.total_amount,0.0) DESC) AS amount_rank
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.customerid AS customerid,
         COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderid) AS total_orders,
         SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0))) AS total_amount
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN order_details od ON od.orderid = o.orderid
  GROUP BY o.customerid
) oagg ON oagg.customerid = c.customerid
accepted.description: One row per customer with their total_orders and total_amount (derived from order_details) and a rank by total_amount descending. Useful for top-customer reporting and downstream filtering by rank to implement Top-K customers. | Use for: Find top customers by revenue; Customer lifetime value and segmentation by total spend; Lists of customers with order counts and spend for CRM actions

accepted.name: employee_sales_running_total
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT o.orderid,
       o.employeeid,
       o.orderdate,
       SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0))) AS order_amount,
       SUM(SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0)))) OVER (PARTITION BY o.employeeid ORDER BY o.orderdate ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total_by_employee
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN order_details od ON od.orderid = o.orderid
GROUP BY o.orderid, o.employeeid, o.orderdate
accepted.description: One row per order (or order line if joined) per employee with cumulative sales_to_date (running total) ordered by orderdate. Useful to analyze employee sales performance over time and compute period-to-date comparisons or time series of cumulative sales. | Use for: Time series of cumulative sales per employee; Period-to-date comparisons and trend visualizations for reps; Detecting whether an employee reached a sales milestone by date
